question: According to the IMF's April 2025 World Economic Outlook, what is India’s projected GDP growth rate for the year 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.062**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India's GDP Growth Rate for 2025:** According to the **IMF's April 2025 World Economic Outlook**, India's projected GDP growth rate for the year 2025 is **0.062 (6.2%)**.
 
• **IMF Report:** The **International Monetary Fund** regularly publishes its **World Economic Outlook (WEO)**, which includes global and country-specific economic projections.
 
• **India’s Economic Performance:** The growth rate of **6.2%** indicates a robust and steady economic performance, showcasing India's resilience amid global economic uncertainties.
 
• **Comparison with Previous Years:** This rate reflects stable growth compared to previous years, aligning with India's ongoing reforms and investments in infrastructure and manufacturing.
 
• **Global Context:** While India remains one of the fastest-growing major economies, this projection also highlights the challenges posed by global inflation, geopolitical tensions, and post-pandemic recovery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IMF's World Economic Outlook (WEO):**

 
 
• The **World Economic Outlook** is published biannually by the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**.
 
• It provides detailed analysis of global economic trends, forecasts, and policy recommendations.
 
• The WEO includes projections for GDP growth rates, inflation, and fiscal balances for various countries.
 
 
 
• **India’s Economic Reforms:**
 
 
• India has implemented several reforms such as **Goods and Services Tax (GST), Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), and Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes** to enhance its economic growth.
 
• Investments in **digital infrastructure**, renewable energy, and urban development have contributed significantly to economic stability.
 
 
 
• **Global Economic Challenges:**
 
 
• Factors like **inflationary pressures**, disruptions in the supply chain, and **geopolitical conflicts** have impacted global growth rates.
 
• India's growth projection remains optimistic despite these challenges, signaling strong domestic demand and policy support.
 
 
 
• **India’s Sectoral Contributions:**
 
 
• Key drivers of economic growth include **agriculture, manufacturing, IT services, and exports**.
 
• India is also focusing on sectors like **green energy**, electric vehicles, and infrastructure development to sustain long-term growth.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **IMF Overview:**

 
 
• The **International Monetary Fund** was established in **1944** and has 190 member countries.
 
• Its primary objectives include promoting global monetary cooperation, securing financial stability, and fostering economic growth.
 
 
 
• **India’s Position in the Global Economy:**
 
 
• India is the **fifth-largest economy** in terms of nominal GDP and the third-largest in purchasing power parity (PPP).
 
• With a population exceeding **1.4 billion**, it has a large and growing consumer base.
 
 
 
• **Economic Indicators to Monitor:**
 
 
• Key metrics to track include **GDP growth rate, inflation rate, fiscal deficit, and foreign exchange reserves**.
 
• These indicators provide a comprehensive understanding of India's economic health and sustainability.
